questions.questionText: What is an example of a macroeconomic aim?

options.text: to create and maintain full employment
to improve efficiency in the manufacturing sector of the economy
to provide consumers with greater information when buying goods and services
to encourage greater occupational mobility of labour

questions.questionText: Why might a market economy fail to achieve the best use of scarce resources?

options.text: Consumers may lack information about which good to buy.
Most resources are owned by the government.

questions.questionText: Which task is not a function of a trade union?

options.text: agreeing the minimum number to be employed on a particular job
deciding on the level of a national minimum wage
negotiating working hours and conditions of work
providing legal advice on unfair dismissal

questions.questionText: What does not have an effect on wages in a free market economy?

options.text: the number of people willing and able to work

whole economy?

options.text: to encourage an increase in production and to prevent high inflation
to ensure no one is unemployed and to reduce exports
to give everyone equal incomes and to increase government revenue

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be the responsibility of a central government?

options.text: the provision of immigration officials at an airport
the provision of security cameras in a shopping centre
the provision of security staff at a bank
the provision of ticket inspectors on a train

questions.questionText:
The government wants to reduce the consumption of cigarettes.
Which policy would be most likely to do this?

options.text: increasing the indirect tax on cigarettes

questions.questionText: Which group should not be included in the measurement of unemployment?

options.text: redundant unskilled workers seeking alternative work
seasonal agricultural workers in out-of-season periods
students over 18 years continuing with full-time education
those who have left school and cannot get a job

questions.questionText:
An economy is experiencing rising prices.
Which government policy will help reduce consumer expenditure?

options.text: introducing compulsory saving for income earners

questions.questionText:
Some goods take a greater percentage of a typical household’s total spending than others.
How is this accounted for in the construction of a consumer prices index?

options.text: by giving a weight to the goods
by taking an average of price fluctuations during a year
by using the price elasticity of demand for the goods

questions.questionText:
In countries with absolute poverty, low incomes can start a process that keeps incomes low.
What are the stages of this process?

options.text: low incomes  low consumption  low prices  low output  low incomes
low incomes  low government spending  high taxation  low employment  low incomes
low incomes  low investment  high profits  low dividends  low incomes
low incomes  low saving  low investment  low productivity  low incomes
